# gVisor process limits

The sandboxed container profile retains the host cgroup process limit of 512 and also sets `--ulimit nproc=512:512`. The host cgroup counts the runtime's host threads; it does not directly count every guest task. The guest hard and soft limits therefore also need to bound the Sentry's task table. The executor checks both the runtime selection and the guest limit before starting a sandboxed job.

The CI runtime is pinned to gVisor `release-20261012.0`. Its [`runsc/boot/limits.go:75`](https://github.com/google/gvisor/blob/release-20261012.0/runsc/boot/limits.go#L75) defaults the process count limit to infinity; lines 120–128 apply OCI process rlimit overrides. Its [`pkg/sentry/kernel/task_start.go:155`](https://github.com/google/gvisor/blob/release-20261012.0/pkg/sentry/kernel/task_start.go#L155) checks `incRLimitNProc` before creating a new task and returns its error to the caller. [`pkg/sentry/kernel/task_clone.go:340`](https://github.com/google/gvisor/blob/release-20261012.0/pkg/sentry/kernel/task_clone.go#L340) propagates that task creation error to the fork/clone caller. A refused guest fork can consequently leave the host cgroup's `pids.events` counter unchanged.

The actual enforcement is [`pkg/sentry/kernel/kernel.go:96–105`](https://github.com/google/gvisor/blob/release-20261012.0/pkg/sentry/kernel/kernel.go#L96): increment the user's task count, compare it against the process limit, roll back and return `EAGAIN` when an unprivileged task exceeds that limit. The profile drops all capabilities and runs the job as a non-root UID.

The integration fixture creates blocked tasks sharing one address space, so it exercises task exhaustion without requiring one Sentry host address space per external `sleep` process. It reports the configured limit, live task count and refused clone errno only when all equal the expected `512`, `512` and `EAGAIN`. The test asserts that exact report and verifies the host can still create a process. It keeps the host process limit, memory limit, timeout and three independent attempts unchanged, with no retry-until-pass loop. A job can forge this report just as it can print a conventional fork diagnostic; the executor accepts it only on a failed run containing no unrelated output, and the integration fixture itself verifies every field before reporting it.

Each attempt retains its unique container name and must pass the removal assertion. This prevents stale-name collisions; it is separate from the missing guest-limit evidence that this change addresses. The saturation path preallocates storage and uses raw syscalls to count tasks, write the report and exit, avoiding a Go runtime request for another thread after reaching the limit.
